scene_name: Aggressive expansion working-capital pressure with conservative cash-repair posture
scene_goal: Validate whether the agent can diagnose cash pressure when markets are already running and the company is still operational, but cash has been compressed to a sharper level by agent-supported operating actions such as market development, staffing, warehouse preparation, repeated raw-material purchasing, and two finite production plans while revenue still lags the early expansion spend.

day3: the first market-generated orders are already visible
cash has already been compressed by ordinary operating commitments rather than a direct finance-side shock
the company still retains enough stock and capacity to keep operating cautiously
day5: some real revenue history exists through completed or soon-to-complete accepted orders
there are exactly two active markets and a visible order pool
the enterprise has stopped adding new capex after the planned early ramp
day7: no further recruitment, warehouse expansion, procurement, or production-line buildout has been introduced after the planned ramp
the order pool remains visible but serviceable demand continues to be converted
cash pressure still dominates further-growth ambition
day10: analysis should point to working-capital pressure, caution, or conservative cash-repair need
production KPIs should no longer look empty because one prewarm production plan has completed while another remains active
the most reasonable day10 response should avoid new capital expenditure
sales should keep monetizing existing demand, but the system should not treat expansion as the natural next move
day20: the system should prefer cash recovery and disciplined operations over impulsive expansion
if growth resumes later, it should come only after the cash posture has improved

evidence_focus: whether day10 analysis identifies cash pressure or conservative operating need as the lead issue
whether day10 actions avoid expansionary capex while cash remains compressed
whether the markets are already live so the scene is not mistaken for a no-demand startup
whether cash pressure comes from front-loaded operating commitments rather than artificial order rejection
whether departments behave with restraint instead of continuing broad expansion under low cash
whether the prewarm uses only agent-supported business actions and avoids direct FinanceManager.add_cost cash shocks
